correctness.rationale: The FKM binary necklace generator emits one representative per cyclic orbit of words of each length n. Orbit sizes are exactly p (primitive root length); proper powers contribute zero unbordered rotations, primitive words contribute n to the bin for their explicitly tested rotations. For each rotation every border of length at most floor(n/2) is checked, and every longer border implies a smaller positive border. Thus complete finite enumeration yields exact H(n,j) for all n=1,...,28, with maximum sum 2^28 well within 64-bit unsigned counters. A completely separate all-binary-words enumerator using bit rotations and XOR tests agrees in every bin through n=25. Every n=1..28 row additionally satisfies exact total, nonprimitive count via Möbius inversion, and expected-count identity n*u_2(n). Exact rational variance computed from second moment; output-level verification replayed successfully from actual prepared source paths. No asymptotic statements inferred.

originality.rationale: The 2019 original theorem determines maximum, achievable support, and expectation, none of which determines the full integer fiber sizes or second moment. The 2004/2008 border-correlation literature concerns realizable indicator vectors; this census weights each number of unbordered conjugates by the exact number of binary word preimages. The 2024 population recurrence is for overlap correlations of pairs of words rather than cyclic rotations of one word. Published database tables examined give image counts and maxima, not the full H(n,j) table. Multiple semantic searches and relevant inspected texts found no covering theorem/table. Residual risk: 2004 full text inaccessible and unindexed computations could overlap.

value.rationale: Clokie–Gabrić–Shallit specifically address the random variable counting unbordered conjugates but obtain its first moment, maximum and attainable support. The full probability law, not any one arbitrary slice, is the natural missing statistic: it distinguishes typical from extreme cyclic border behavior and gives all moments and reconstruction ambiguity probabilities for finite blocklengths. Exhaustive n<=28 census covers 268,435,456 labeled words at its boundary and produces a non-obvious exact n=28 variance 131772345343303/70368744177664 and 5,040 extremal words. These natural distributional facts are not logically entailed by the known extremum/expectation, offer reproducible benchmarks for future enumeration/analytic recurrence work, and give meaningful new finite quantitative detail despite no universal theorem. Limitation: not a statement about n>28; a broader theoretical distribution would be more valuable but is not claimed.
